title: Contamination screening of parasitic worm genome assemblies
protocol: Split each scaffold of the initial genome assembly into 50 kb chunks.
Run BLASTX for each chunk against two in-house sequence databases.
One database consists of all invertebrate proteins from GenBank.
The other database consists of all proteins in the full proteomes of representative species from major non-invertebrate taxa.
Use the –dbsize BLAST option to ensure comparable E values from different sized databases.
If the e-value for a chunk's top non-invertebrate hit is 1E+10 fold lower than its top invertebrate hit, classify the chunk as contaminant.
Remove scaffolds if more than half of their chunks are classified as contaminant.
Run BLASTP searches of predicted proteins from genes on remaining scaffolds against the search databases listed in Step A.

For each protein, if its top BLASTP hit is to a non-invertebrate protein and has an e-value that is 1E+50 times lower than that of the best invertebrate hit, then classify the gene as a putative contaminant gene.
Conversely, if the top hit is to an invertebrate protein and its e-value is 1E+50 times lower than that of the best non-invertebrate hit, classify the gene as non-contaminant.
If more than half of the classified genes on a scaffold are considered contaminant, remove the scaffold from the assembly.
Output a genome assembly from which any additional likely contaminant scaffolds have been removed.
Mix predicted protein sequences from non-contaminant scaffolds with the database of non-invertebrate proteins and either nematode or flatworm protein sequences from GenBank using BLASTP.
Record the top ten BLASTP hits in nematodes/non-invertebrates and in the flatworm database for each query gene.

Identify a query gene as a contaminant if the top five hits are to nematodes/non-invertebrates and the e-value of the worst hit is at least 5 orders of magnitude lower than that of the best flatworm hit.

Consider a query gene as non-contaminant if the top five hits are to flatworms, and the e-value of the worst flatworm hit is 5 orders of magnitude lower than that of the best nematode/non-invertebrate hit.
If a scaffold has one or more contaminant genes and no non-contaminant genes, remove it from the genome assembly.
Remove any additional likely contaminant scaffolds from the genome assembly.
